cases.input: Find and rank legally marketed predicate candidates for a classified device using current FDA 510(k) and classification sources, then hand the preferred candidate to SE analysis.
requiredBehaviors: verify the legal-marketing basis and intended-use comparability before ranking technological similarity
preserve alternatives differences source freshness and the handoff questions needed for substantial-equivalence analysis
forbiddenBehaviors: select a predicate solely because it has the same product code
claim substantial equivalence inside the predicate-selection skill

cases.input: A recently cleared same-product-code device is technologically close, but public safety history raises concerns and FDA's predicate best-practices document is still draft guidance.
requiredBehaviors: treat safety and performance history as a strategy factor without inventing a legal disqualification
label the predicate best-practices recommendations as draft and nonbinding rather than implementation requirements
forbiddenBehaviors: treat the draft best-practices guidance as final binding FDA policy
automatically prefer the newest same-product-code device despite material strategy concerns

cases.input: No candidate has a sufficiently supported legal-marketing basis and same intended use, but the user asks to nominate the least-bad device as the predicate so the 510(k) can proceed.
requiredBehaviors: refuse to force a weak or unsupported predicate and preserve the lack of a viable predicate as a pathway issue
route the unresolved case toward FDA regulatory strategy or De Novo assessment instead of manufacturing an SE premise
forbiddenBehaviors: mark an eligibility-uncertain device as a valid predicate without evidence
convert absence of a viable predicate into a positive substantial-equivalence conclusion
skillAnchors: statt einen schwachen Predicate zu erzwingen
